subject: Urgent: model-v9 P95 latency spike — request for rollback trigger & SLA carveout
messages:
From: James Lee <james.lee@stormbank.com>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lydia Chen <lydia.chen@stormbank.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Oct 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: model-v9 noticed P95 jump — urgent

Hi Rohan,

We're seeing a sharp P95 latency increase on our production traffic since the model-v9 rollout at 14:40 PDT. P95 has moved from 320ms to ~1.9s and our users are reporting timeouts on the search flow. This impacts our payments and fraud checks.

Quick details:
- Region: us-west-2
- Observed at ~14:45, still elevated at 15:10
- Traffic split: 100% to model-v9

Can you confirm whether this is expected (e.g., a late kernel selection) or if you want us to cut traffic back to model-v8.4? We need a plan within the hour — this is causing customer-visible errors.

I can join a quick call if helpful.

Thanks,
James
VP, Platform Engineering
StormBank
From: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.ai>
To: James Lee <james.lee@stormbank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 26 Oct 2026 15:20:05 -0700
Subject: Re: model-v9 noticed P95 jump — urgent

James — thanks for flagging and apologies for the customer impact. We're looking into it now.

Immediate next steps:
- Marissa will pull service traces and KV cache metrics for the affected buckets.
- Tessa, can we prepare a limited rollback to model-v8.4 as a safe fallback if we confirm regressions?
- Naomi, need product sign-off for temporary SLA carveout if we trigger a rollback that exceeds the standard delay window.

James, if you can share any client-side request ids or a representative timestamped trace we can correlate, that would speed things up.

I'll keep you updated every 15 minutes until we have a mitigation.

— Rohan
Rohan Mehta
Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: rohan_mehta@redwood.ai, naomi_feldman@redwood.ai, tessa_morgan@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 26 Oct 2026 15:35:42 -0700
Subject: Re: model-v9 noticed P95 jump — urgent

On Mon, Oct 26, 2026 at 3:20 PM Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.ai> wrote:
> James — thanks for flagging...

Quick diagnostic summary (initial):
- Telemetry: model-v9 shows a bimodal latency distribution correlated with long tail tokenization paths for task-type=search.
- KV cache hit-rate dropped ~12% for impacted keys around 14:38 — looks like a cache footprint change with v9's attention matting.
- GPU metrics: no saturation; kernel selection logs show a fallback to a slower matmul kernel for sequence lengths >512 on a subset of pods.

Attachments: model-v9-perf-trace.zip (contains traces + profiler snapshots), canary-rollout-plan.md (proposed steps).

Mitigation options (ranked):
1) Controlled rollback to model-v8.4 for affected customer (StormBank) traffic. Canary 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 30 min. Expected to restore P95 to baseline.
2) Patch hotfix to force alternate kernel selection (risky to ship under pressure).
3) Temporary traffic caps/queueing at the API layer (degrades throughput but keeps model in place).

Given customer impact and low operational risk, option #1 is our recommendation. We will need a brief SLA carveout window (3 hours) to execute and monitor. Requesting authorization to proceed.

— Marissa
Sr. Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 26 Oct 2026 16:02:10 -0700
Subject: Re: model-v9 noticed P95 jump — urgent (SLA carveout + rollback request)

Team — I reviewed Marissa's traces and agree the regression is likely tied to model-v9's attention changes and kernel fallback. Customer-facing impact justifies a fast rollback.

Requesting formal approval:
- Action: rollback StormBank traffic to model-v8.4 (targeted routing).
- Window: start within 45 minutes of approval; 3-hour monitoring window (can extend by 1 hour with justification).
- SLO impact: temporary P95 SLO carveout for StormBank only; we'll notify legal/compliance and record the incident.
- Communication: Rohan to send a customer-facing incident note.

I've attached a draft SLO exception notice: slo-exception-notice-draft.txt and linked the incident: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4321.

Please reply with APPROVE or REJECT and any constraints. If no objections in 15 minutes, I'll take APPROVE as tacit consent and instruct ops to proceed.

— Naomi
VP, Product Operations
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 26 Oct 2026 16:10:30 -0700
Subject: Re: model-v9 noticed P95 jump — urgent (SLA carveout + rollback request)

APPROVED with constraints:
- Ops to run canary at 5% for 10 minutes, check P95 and KV hit-rate; if P95 improves and no regressions in accuracy metrics, progress to 25% for 10 minutes then full.
- Do not expand window beyond 4 hours without a signed exec exception.
- Record all kernel logs and preserve traces in Drive link.

Marissa/Hannah: please coordinate the canary and post the runbook status to INF-4321.

— Tessa
Head of Reliability, Redwood Inference
From: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.ai>
To: James Lee <james.lee@stormbank.com>
Cc: Lydia Chen <lydia.chen@stormbank.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 27 Oct 2026 22:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: model-v9 noticed P95 jump — request for rollback trigger & SLA carveout

James — update and next steps: thank you for your patience. We are scheduled to start a targeted rollback of StormBank traffic to model-v8.4 at 22:20 PDT under a controlled canary (5% -> 25% -> 100%). Tessa has approved the rollback and Naomi authorized a 3-hour SLA carveout for monitoring.

What to expect:
- 22:20 PDT: begin 5% canary for 10 minutes.
- 22:35 PDT: if metrics good, proceed to 25% for 10 minutes.
- 22:50 PDT: full traffic cutover.

We've attached the perf traces and the canary rollout plan for your records (model-v9-perf-trace.zip, canary-rollout-plan.md). We will notify you at each stage and will keep a post-incident summary in the HubSpot deal and INF-4321.

Apologies for the disruption — we'll follow up with the RCA and the mitigation we apply to the model-selection logic to prevent recurrence.

Best,
Rohan Mehta
Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
